newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota, Matsushita form battery venture.
newsitem.headline: Toyota, Matsushita form battery venture.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp and Matsushita Electric Industrial Co said on Wednesday they had officially set up a joint venture to develop, make and sell nickel-metal hydride rechargeable batteries for electric vehicles.
Plans to form the venture were announced in May.
The new company, Panasonic EV Energy Co Ltd, will be capitalised at two billion yen and will be owned 60 percent by Matsushita group firms and 40 percent by Toyota.

The new company will begin operations in January 1997 and will produce 5,000 to 10,000 units per year during its first three years, with hopes of achieving annual sales of 20 billion yen by the year 1999, a Toyota spokesman said.
The venture's batteries will be marketed to car makers both in Japan and abroad.
Toyota began selling electric cars in Japan in September, although the battery venture hopes to achieve greater economies of scale by selling to Toyota rivals as well.
